title: KV segment rotation and proactive shear rewrite (fragmentation mitigation)
creator: Priya Raman
description: Investigate and implement a KV cache allocation strategy that uses segment rotation plus a proactive 'shear rewrite' mechanism to reduce long-term fragmentation on GPU memory without introducing observable latency spikes during continuous batching workloads.
background: We observe gradual GPU KV cache fragmentation on long-running dedicated pods serving chat and long-context generation workloads. Fragmentation increases allocation failures for high-length requests and raises the need for larger soft reserves, negatively affecting throughput and unit cost. Existing approaches (aggressive compaction, epochal pauses) either introduce latency spikes or are insufficient under continuous batching patterns.
goal: Design and deploy a low-latency background compaction/reshuffle mechanism that: 1) reduces free space fragmentation by ~60% in steady-state, 2) keeps p99 generation latency impact < 1ms, and 3) limits additional GPU memory bandwidth to < 8% of baseline for typical workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation ratio (max-free-run / total-free) reduced by >= 60% in 24h steady-state test
No regression in tail token latency: p95 and p99 within 1ms of baseline under continuous batching
Allocation failure rate reduced by >= 70% for model contexts >= 8k tokens
Telemetry added: per-GPU fragment heatmap, rotation throughput, shear-rewrite bytes, and per-model relocation counts
Incremental rollout plan with feature flag and automatic backoff on latency spikes
proposed_solution: Introduce a 'segment rotation' controller that periodically promotes low-occupancy segments to a relocation queue and compacts hot entries into freshly allocated contiguous segments using a 'shear rewrite' operator. The operator performs in-place-style relocation by allocating a new contiguous segment, copying live KV entries (KV shard + token ranges) into the new slab using GPU-friendly batched copies, then atomically swapping segment descriptors. A background scheduler coordinates with the continuous batching runtime to schedule low-priority relocation slices between micro-batches to avoid interference. We add per-segment metadata: occupancy, age, relocation_score, and a lightweight churn fingerprint to avoid re-relocating highly volatile tokens repeatedly.
detailed_design: Segment metadata: occupancy_count, live_size_bytes, avg_age, last_moved_ts, relocation_score
Relocation scoring: score = alpha * (1 - occupancy_ratio) + beta * age_normalized + gamma * frag_penalty where frag_penalty measures adjacent free runs

Shear rewrite algorithm: (1) reserve contiguous segment N bytes (soft-reserve), (2) produce relocation plan of KV entries ordered by decreasing size for coalescing, (3) launch batched GPU memcpy kernels with pinned host staging for NVLINK-less pods, (4) update segment table with CAS to avoid races, (5) free old segment space and update free-run map

Concurrency model: relocation uses cooperative preemption at micro-batch boundaries. During a relocation slice the runtime yields for up to a configurable token window (e.g., 256 tokens) and resumes. If scheduler detects increased latency, relocation slices exponentially back off.

Soft-reserve and fallback: maintain a per-GPU soft-reserve pool so allocation failures can fall back to eviction-based compaction. If soft-reserve is depleted, prioritize eviction of least-recently-accessed entries and postpone relocation until reclaim completes.
Wear-leveling: track per-token relocation counters and penalize tokens with high relocation_count to avoid repeated moves. Introduce a cool-down TTL for re-relocation attempts.
Telemetry: per-segment histograms, relocation bytes/sec, average relocation slice duration, p50/p95/p99 latency impact tags, and eviction vs relocation ratio
Safety: relocate only if contiguous destination segment available above a min_size threshold; fallback to partial compaction (move hot subset) if contiguous not found
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype relocation controller in runtime sandbox (2 days): metric hooks, segment metadata, scoring function adjustable via flags
2) Implement shear-rewrite operator (6 days): batched copy paths, CAS segment descriptor swap, staged host buffers for non-NVLINK nodes
3) Integrate scheduler hooks to batcher (3 days): cooperative preemption at micro-batch boundaries and backoff signals
4) Add telemetry and dashboards (2 days): fragment heatmap, relocation throughput, latency tagging
5) Internal canary on dedicated test cluster with synthetic churn workloads (4 days): tune alpha/beta/gamma and slice sizing
6) Gradual rollout behind feature flag to low-traffic tenants (7 days), monitor and iterate
7) Global rollout and post-release evaluation (3 days)
telemetry_and_metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency delta with feature on
rollout_plan: Start with an opt-in flag for dedicated customers. Run 48h synthetic workload test with tenant-level throttles. Canary to 5% of dedicated pods, monitor p99 latency, allocation failures, and GPU memory bandwidth. If metrics stable, ramp to 25% then 100% over 2-3 weeks; include automated rollback when p99 increases beyond threshold or allocation failures spike.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: relocation causes CPU/GPU bandwidth contention and increases tail latency. Mitigation: cooperative preemption, dynamic slice sizing, and immediate backoff signals from batcher.
Risk: repeated relocation of hot tokens (oscillation). Mitigation: relocation_count-based cool-down, wear-leveling penalty, and hot-token pinning for short TTLs.
Risk: lack of contiguous destination space leads to many small moves. Mitigation: preferentially allocate destination from soft-reserve and fall back to partial compaction ordering by entry size.

Risk: complexity in atomic swap semantics across multi-GPU model shards. Mitigation: design segment descriptor versioning and two-phase commit for cross-shard relocations with lightweight locks and retry loops.
Risk: NVLINK/PCIe heterogeneity causing variable copy throughput. Mitigation: runtime detects topology and selects optimal copy path (peer-to-peer vs host-staged) and adaptive slice sizing
open_questions: What is the ideal default for alpha/beta/gamma in the relocation scoring function for the majority of workloads?
Should we expose relocation aggressiveness as a tenant-level knob or keep it internal?
How large should the per-GPU soft-reserve be relative to model working set (fixed % or adaptive)?
Cross-tenant vs per-tenant relocation: should we isolate relocation pools to tenant-level to avoid noisy neighbors?
notes: Design inspired by segment rotation patterns used in flash wear-leveling and LSM tree compaction heuristics.
Compared to full defragmentation, shear rewrite aims to move only the hot subset to a contiguous destination to reduce bandwidth and risk.
Will coordinate with Optimize team to surface recommended settings based on observed workload fingerprints.
Plan to add a simulator that replays trace logs to estimate fragmentation improvements before enabling on production pods.
references: Paper: "Compaction Techniques for LSM Trees" (background reference)
